## The golden receipts are blessed

Unlike the canonical goldens, a receipt can only be produced by running the engine, so the five
`*.receipt.json` goldens are written by the crate's bless switch and reviewed. Each embeds the
engine version (inside its `receipt_id`) and its subject's content id, so a workspace version
bump re-blesses all five, and so does re-vendoring either rule (#517), which also re-makes the
three mutants. Their `receipt_id` is not
taken on trust: `tests/receipt_goldens.rs` cuts the `receipt_id` line and the `timings` block out
of each golden's text and hashes the rest with a second FNV-1a-128, which must give the id the
golden holds.

## The canonical goldens are not blessed

`tests/canonical_form.rs` compares `VectorSet::to_canonical_json` with the files under
`canonical/` byte for byte and `VectorSet::spec_id` with literals in the test. Neither was produced
by this crate, and no switch rewrites them: a golden made by the code it checks cannot fail.

[`derive_canonical.py`](derive_canonical.py) derives them. It is a second implementation of the
canonical form and of FNV-1a-128, in Python, sharing no code with the crate:

- it reads the document with `json.load`, keeping an integer token and a real apart
  (`parse_int`, `parse_float`);
- it writes every object's keys sorted by `key.encode("utf-8")`, two-space indentation, one entry
  per line, `{}` and `[]` for empty ones, and one final line feed;
- it writes a string with `\"`, `\\` and `\n`, printable ASCII as it is, and every other character
  as `\u` and four lowercase hex digits per UTF-16 unit;
- it writes an integer with `str`, and a real with `repr` (Python's shortest round-trip digits,
  which switch to an exponent outside `1e-4 <= |x| < 1e16` as the note's rule does), respelling
  the exponent from `e-05` and `e+16` to `e-5` and `e16`;
- it hashes the bytes with FNV-1a-128 over Python integers and prints `spec:fnv1a128:<32 hex>`.

No test runs it. When the format changes in place, run it by hand from this directory for each
golden, review the diff, update the id literals in `tests/canonical_form.rs`, and say in the pull
request which bytes moved and why:

```bash
python3 -I derive_canonical.py sets/every_field.json canonical/every_field.json
python3 -I derive_canonical.py \
  ../../../../oce-api/tests/fixtures/library_rules/AHU-0016/vectors.json canonical/AHU-0016.json
python3 -I derive_canonical.py \
  ../../../../oce-api/tests/fixtures/library_rules/AHU-0004/vectors.json canonical/AHU-0004.json
```
